findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the container-case handling: either exclude container-criterion cases whose eval spec supplies no `children` (as `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` does not, per eval_solver.py:110-116), or pick a runnable anchor worked example, so the ItemRecord adapter contract is demonstrable and the gold count is not silently eroded.
evidence: Plan worked example: 'dataset case G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar in plan-review-container.eval.yaml ... its three v2 epochs return findings / findings / no-findings ... ItemRecord(valid=True, decision="block", label="block")'
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:110-116 — container criterion with no non-empty `children` list raises ValueError
Verified: `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` dataset has zero `children` keys (search returned no matches); cases carry only id/corpus/criterion/expect/note/input
Contrast: `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` DOES carry `children`, so the runnability discriminator is the spec, not the criterion — the blanket 'criterion arm' rule cannot distinguish them
Plan names `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` as the largest gold source (12)
findings.finding: The eligibility rule admits `plan-review-container` G3/G4 cases, but that spec supplies no `children` payload, so `_run_criterion_case` raises ValueError for a container criterion on every epoch — and the plan's own anchor worked example (`G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar`) is one of these cases, making its claimed ItemRecord derivation impossible as written.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' worked example, and the ItemRecord-adapter contract
scenarios: The sampler draws the first finding case of the largest gold spec (a container case with no children); every epoch on both arms raises ValueError, so the anchor example's block/block record can never form.
findings.suggested_fix: Require, in the eligibility rule, that a container-criterion case carry a non-empty `children` list (which admits `plan-review-decomp-shape` cases and excludes `plan-review-container` cases as written), and replace the `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` worked example with a case that actually runs — e.g. a `decomp-shape` fixture that carries children.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether provider_parity.py IMPORTS `_verdict_decision` and `_majority_decision` from fidelity_spot_eval (or a shared module) rather than re-implementing them; if promoting them out of the plan_review package for cross-package reuse, name the shared home.
evidence: Plan: 'the same two-bucket mapping fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision already uses'
Plan: 'reduces to a majority decision (ties broken toward the cautious block), exactly as fidelity_spot_eval.relocation_spot_eval(epochs=…) and _majority_decision already do'
fidelity_spot_eval.py:79 `_verdict_decision` and :127 `_majority_decision` are provider-agnostic pure helpers (no plan-review coupling), already exercised by tests/unit/test_fidelity_spot_eval.py
Both helpers are module-private (leading underscore) but importable within the same package
findings.finding: The two pure overlap helpers `_verdict_decision` and `_majority_decision` are referenced by behavior ('the same two-bucket mapping fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision already uses'; 'exactly as ... _majority_decision already do') rather than by explicit import-and-reuse, leaving it ambiguous whether the new module re-implements them — which would be a small NIH copy of already-tested pure functions.
findings.location: Plan sections 'Corpus and the gold floor' and 'Repeats'; Scope bullet for src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py
scenarios: Author re-implements the block/advisory mapping and ties-toward-block majority in provider_parity.py, then the two copies drift (e.g. a future change to the cautious-tie rule updates only one)
findings.suggested_fix: Import `_verdict_decision` and `_majority_decision` from `rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval` (or lift them to a small shared parity-helpers module) instead of re-writing the two-bucket mapping and majority reducer in the new module.

findings.finding: The step-1 probe's failure handling assumes all-or-nothing invokability, but the two class slots depend on independent inference-profile ids; the plan does not resolve the partial-invokability case where the sonnet (standard) profile is invokable but no opus (frontier) profile is.
findings.location: Approach — 'Riskiest assumption, tested first' and 'Arms and pairing'
findings.suggested_fix: Make the probe per-slot: if a slot's id is invokable, run that slot; if the frontier id is refused, record the exact refusal as the frontier finding, run the standard slot, and treat 'frontier unmeasured' as a criterion the epic's first-class claim must resolve — not a silent sonnet-only pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the selection rule when a spec lacks one gold bucket (take whatever is available; do not require the pair) and describe the count as "up to 30, floor 20" rather than a fixed 15/15, or assert in the offline corpus test that all 15 specs do supply both buckets.
evidence: "the first finding/fail case and the first pass case per spec, ordered by spec id then case id — 30 items, 15 gold-block and 15 gold-advisory"
If any spec has no eligible `pass` case (or no eligible `finding`/`fail` case), the per-spec pair is incomplete and the 30/15/15 counts silently do not hold.
findings.finding: The corpus selector's exact yield ("30 items, 15 gold-block and 15 gold-advisory") assumes every one of the 15 specs contributes both a finding/fail case and a pass case; the plan does not state the behavior when a spec's eligible pool lacks one bucket.
findings.location: Approach → Corpus and the gold floor
scenarios: A spec with only block-labelled gold cases yields one item, not two; the recorded corpus digest then has fewer than 30 items and an unbalanced block/advisory split.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fixed "30 items, 15/15" phrasing with "one finding/fail and one pass case per spec where each exists (up to 30 items; the floor is 20 gold)", and have the corpus-exclusion offline test assert the actual per-bucket counts rather than assume 15/15.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the corpus-eligibility rule (or add an explicit exclusion) so `plan-review-isf-finder` ISF cases, which `_run_criterion_case` raises ValueError on (eval_solver.py:131-135), are excluded rather than admitted as guaranteed-errored records; state the fallback for a case that raises on 100% of epochs.
evidence: Plan: 'A case is eligible when its `expect` is in {finding, fail, pass} AND its solver id ... resolves to a non-agentic run_case arm'
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:131-135 — `if cid == "ISF": raise ValueError(... is an ISF finder (needs a session log), not runnable over an inline eval fixture)`
src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-isf-finder.eval.yaml:42-56 — ISF-R1/ISF-F1 carry `criterion` implicit (prompt: plan-review-isf-finder) with `expect: finding`/`pass`
The ISF criterion arm IS a non-agentic run_case arm (the criterion arm), so the plan's rule does not exclude it
findings.finding: The corpus-eligibility rule admits `plan-review-isf-finder` cases (expect: finding/pass, criterion: ISF), but `_run_criterion_case` raises ValueError for the ISF criterion on every epoch of both arms, so they enter the corpus as guaranteed-errored records with no specified handling.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' (eligibility rule) and 'Error classification'
scenarios: The stratified sampler picks the first finding case for the ISF spec (ISF-R1) and the first pass case (ISF-F1); both raise on every epoch on both arms, entering as errored ItemRecords.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ISF to the exclusion set alongside the three agentic specs, or make eligibility require that the resolved arm can actually run the case shape (e.g. exclude criterion==ISF), and specify that a case erroring on all epochs of both arms is dropped from the sample rather than recorded as an errored gold item.
